lesson_scope: Integer powers in polar and exponential forms, powers on real and imaginary axes, multiple-angle trigonometric derivations via Euler identities, roots of complex power equations, and geometric configurations in Argand diagrams.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Squaring a complex number in exponential polar form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Squaring a complex number and expressing in exponential form.

walkthrough.text:
Find modulus and argument of $z$:
$$|z| = \sqrt{(\sqrt{3})^2 + (-1)^2} = 2, \quad \arg(z) = -\arctan\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{6} \implies z = 2\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{6}\mathrm{i}}$$

Square the complex number in exponential form:
$$z^2 = (2\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{3}\mathrm{i}/2})^2 = 4\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{3}\mathrm{i}}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Cubing a complex number with principal argument range adjustment.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Cubing exponential form and reducing argument.

walkthrough.text:
Cube the complex number and adjust argument:
$$w^3 = (\sqrt{2})^3 \mathrm{e}^{\frac{9\pi}{4}\mathrm{i}} = 2\sqrt{2}\mathrm{e}^{\left(\frac{9\pi}{4}-2\pi\right)\mathrm{i}} = 2\sqrt{2}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\pi}{4}\mathrm{i}}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Evaluating negative integer power in exponential form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Negative integer power in exponential form.

walkthrough.text:
Multiply angle by $-2$ and adjust to principal range:
$$\text{Angle} = -2 \times \frac{2\pi}{3} = -\frac{4\pi}{3}$$
$$\theta = -\frac{4\pi}{3} + 2\pi = \frac{2\pi}{3} \implies u^{-2} = \frac{1}{4}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2\pi}{3}\mathrm{i}}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Exact Cartesian evaluation of 6th power using polar form.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: High power evaluation via polar coordinates.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Finding smallest integer for purely imaginary power.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding smallest integer exponent for axis alignment.

walkthrough.text:
Set argument to positive imaginary axis:
$$\frac{n\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{2} \implies n = 3$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Finding smallest integer for positive real power.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding smallest integer exponent for positive real power.

walkthrough.text:
Solve for smallest positive integer $n$ making the argument a multiple of $2\pi$:
$$\frac{2n\pi}{3} = 2\pi \implies n = 3$$
$$w^3 = 2^3 \mathrm{e}^{2\pi\mathrm{i}} = 8$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Polar square and modulus-argument condition solving.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Expressing square in exponential polar form.
Finding unknown complex number from modulus ratio and real product.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: 5th power calculation and quotient evaluation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding 5th power in exponential form.
Dividing power by pure imaginary number.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Polar powers and geometric series of roots of unity.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: High powers of 8th root of unity.
Summing geometric series of roots of unity.

hints: Use the geometric series formula $S = \frac{1 - z^8}{1 - z}$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the geometric series sum formula:
$$S = 1 + z + z^2 + \dots + z^7 = \frac{1 - z^8}{1 - z}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses geometric series formula $S = \frac{1 - z^8}{1 - z}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Finding cube roots and computing geometric area of root polygon.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding all 3 cube roots of purely imaginary number.

walkthrough.text:
Express right-hand side in exponential form:
$$8\mathrm{i} = 8\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\pi}{2}\mathrm{i}}$$

Find roots using $r = 8^{1/3} = 2$ and $\theta = \frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{2k\pi}{3}$ for $k = 0, 1, -1$:
$$w_1 = 2\mathrm{e}^{\frac{\pi}{6}\mathrm{i}}, \quad w_2 = 2\mathrm{e}^{\frac{5\pi}{6}\mathrm{i}}, \quad w_3 = 2\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\pi}{2}\mathrm{i}}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Converting roots to Cartesian and finding area of root triangle.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate area of the equilateral triangle:
$$\text{Base} = \sqrt{3} - (-\sqrt{3}) = 2\sqrt{3}$$
$$\text{Height} = 1 - (-2) = 3$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times 2\sqrt{3} \times 3 = 3\sqrt{3}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Proving Euler power identities and expanding (z + 1/z)^4 for multiple angles.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving z^n + 1/z^n and z^n - 1/z^n relations.

walkthrough.text:
Express $z^n$ and $z^{-n}$ in trigonometric form:
$$z^n = \cos(n\theta) + \mathrm{i}\sin(n\theta)$$
$$\frac{1}{z^n} = z^{-n} = \cos(-n\theta) + \mathrm{i}\sin(-n\theta) = \cos(n\theta) - \mathrm{i}\sin(n\theta)$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Binomial expansion of (z + 1/z)^4 to linearise cos^4(theta).

walkthrough.text:
Substitute multiple angle formulas and divide by 16:
$$16\cos^4\theta = 2\cos(4\theta) + 4(2\cos(2\theta)) + 6 = 2\cos(4\theta) + 8\cos(2\theta) + 6$$
$$\cos^4\theta = \frac{1}{8}\cos(4\theta) + \frac{1}{2}\cos(2\theta) + \frac{3}{8}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Polar power axis conditions and modulus-argument equation solving.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Expressing power in polar form and finding negative real condition.

walkthrough.text:
Set condition for negative real axis:
$$\frac{n\pi}{4} = \pi \implies n = 4$$
$$z^4 = 2^2 \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\pi} = -4$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving for modulus and argument from product and quotient equations.

hints: Add $2\pi$ to adjust to principal range $(-\pi, \pi]$: $\arg(w) = \frac{2\pi}{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate and adjust principal argument of $w$:
$$\arg(w) + \arg(z^4) = -\frac{\pi}{3} \implies \arg(w) + \pi = -\frac{\pi}{3}$$
$$\arg(w) = -\frac{4\pi}{3} \equiv -\frac{4\pi}{3} + 2\pi = \frac{2\pi}{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Adds $2\pi$ to adjust $-\frac{4\pi}{3}$ into principal range.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Deriving triple-angle sine formula from polar powers and solving cubic polynomial.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Deriving triple-angle identity via complex binomial cube.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute Euler multiple-angle formulas and solve for $\sin^3\theta$:
$$-8\mathrm{i}\sin^3\theta = 2\mathrm{i}\sin(3\theta) - 6\mathrm{i}\sin\theta$$
$$\sin^3\theta = \frac{3}{4}\sin\theta - \frac{1}{4}\sin(3\theta)$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Substituting specific angle to establish cubic polynomial root.
Factorising cubic equation to find all distinct roots.

hints: Divide $4x^3 - 3x + 1$ by $(2x - 1)$ to obtain quadratic factor $2x^2 + x - 1$.
State $(2x - 1)^2 (x + 1) = 0$, giving the other distinct root $x = -1$.

walkthrough.text:
Factorise the quadratic factor:
$$2x^2 + x - 1 = (2x - 1)(x + 1)$$
$$(2x - 1)^2 (x + 1) = 0$$
$$\text{The distinct roots are } x = \frac{1}{2} \text{ (repeated) and } x = -1$$

ai_rubric.observable: Divides by $(2x - 1)$ to get quadratic factor $2x^2 + x - 1$.
